picks.style: late roman peace-hymn, cithara and soft low strings, clear tenor, flowing, pastoral, unhurried
picks.why: The sword beaten into a curved sickle and the traveller asking which bank Rome rules — the one passage here that is an image rather than a boast.

picks.style: late antique epithalamium, aulos and lyre with light hand drums, bright massed voices, processional, joyful
picks.why: A wedding song complete in itself: pools of honey, rivers of milk, and Europe and Asia lifting torches against each other.

picks.style: late roman martial ode, war horns and deep frame drums, declamatory bass, cold, driving, stark
picks.why: Winter campaign verse that ends on ploughshares ringing against the bones of buried kings — concrete and terrible.

picks.style: latin epic recitation, kithara and bowed strings, warm baritone, supple, tender, hushed
picks.why: Thetis dressing her son as a girl, 'even as the wax that shall live beneath an artist's thumb' — a whole transformation in one image.

picks.style: greek-latin pastoral lament, panpipe and low lyre, mournful mixed voices, slow, receding, elegiac
picks.why: Chiron watching the wake die on the water while the Fauns ask for the boy's songs — the saddest thing in the poem.

picks.style: latin farewell aria, harp and sustained strings, grieving soprano, slow, swelling, salt-heavy
picks.why: Deidamia on the tower going out with the strait until only the poop is left — a departure scene that needs no context.

picks.style: english renaissance-revival hymn, viol consort and recorder, pure tenor, stately, archaic, strophic
picks.why: Mercy at Jove's right hand wafting Virtue's silent tear to heaven's star-throne — a complete Spenserian stanza that stands alone.

picks.style: archaic pastoral ballad, lute and bowed lyre, plain male voice, measured, fable-telling, cool
picks.why: Two transformations in one breath: 'A wolf in form as erst a wolf in soul' and the good man set among the stars.

picks.style: georgian reflective air, harpsichord and cello, grave baritone, measured, sombre, inward
picks.why: 'The mind not taught to think ... dreads the vacant hour' — the mighty void within, in clean couplets.

picks.style: english pastoral folk ballad, acoustic guitar and low flute, warm female vocal, lilting, dreaming, unhurried
picks.why: The moss-floored cottage, the nightingale on the roof, roving with Spenser through a fairy grove — octosyllabics already built to be sung.

picks.style: georgian pastoral ode, chamber strings and oboe, declamatory tenor, spacious, blank-verse cadence, sunlit
picks.why: 'Ye green-rob'd Dryads' — the thrush-haunted copse and the bees humming drowsy lullabies out of a hollow oak.

picks.style: gothic lament, solo viola and dark harp, low troubled voice, slow, unsettled, funereal
picks.why: The address to Despair: the poisoned dagger, the sea-beat mountain's height, the cave to starve and die in.

picks.style: english ballad air, fiddle and plucked cittern, plain warm tenor, brisk, strophic, storytelling
picks.why: 'Remote from citys liv'd a Swain' — four-beat couplets, a whole portrait in ten lines, an opening that opens.

picks.style: wry moral ballad, harpsichord and pizzicato strings, sly baritone, trotting, epigrammatic, light
picks.why: The crab beside the coral grove deciding the ocean was made for his pleasure — the fable's whole point in one image.

picks.style: macabre processional ballad, low organ and muffled drum, dark chorus, slow, tolling, ceremonious
picks.why: Death holding court in his pomp of terrors with Diseases crowding the hall — a court scene that sings itself.

picks.style: english comic ballad, fiddle and hurdy-gurdy, dry mocking tenor, bouncing, brisk, punchline-timed
picks.why: The suicide talked out of the pond because his lice depend on him — a complete joke with a real sting: 'On great folks thus the little live.'

picks.style: renaissance art song, lute and viol, countertenor, reverent, chamber, gently building
picks.why: The Shakespeare cento closing on 'we ne'er shall look upon his like again' — borrowed lines, but it lands as a finished elegy.

picks.style: ancient greek hymnic chant, lyre and deep drone, grave male voice, slow, awestruck, sparse
picks.why: Phidias naming his master: the nod of Cronos' son, the ambrosial locks streaming, Olympus made to tremble.

picks.style: victorian devotional hymn, chamber organ and viola, plaintive alto, slow, aching, congregational
picks.why: 'Our past still travels with us from afar' into 'a thousand years in Thy sight are but as yesterday' — three quotations that make one song about time.

picks.style: balinese kidung chant, gender wayang metallophones and bamboo flute, low male recitation, slow, hypnotic, ritual
picks.why: The only candidate, but a true sloka: matter the cart, the soul the bull, the Lord the charioteer, the world a spinning wheel.
